Thoughts on Duo Lingo: good, bad, ugly?

I like duolingo so far. Once you get to a certain point you will be spending some time strengthening weaknesses on previous lessons which may slow down progress to more advanced areas but I don't necessarily see that as bad.

After a certain point the ratio of time spent refreshing skills vs. time spent learning new skills is too high for me. Having only 30-45 minutes a day to study makes it much more difficult to achieve gold in all skills and actually make progress.

You don't have to keep your tree gold. Nothing prevents you from speeding through the tree. Or you can alternate between strengthening and learning new lessons, depending how you feel on any given day.

I wish they would have more languages open for user contribution. I suppose it streamlines the progress of the few languages that they have users developing, but it would be so much nicer if there was more of a choice.

The contributions of languages is 100% user-based. If you speak, let's say, Icelandic, you can round up a few friends, go to the Duolingo team and ask them to give you permission to start building an Icelandic course.

The course creation is 100% user contribution, but in my opinion it wouldn't be viable to have it completely open for anybody to contribute, because there would be a lot more mistakes in the translations by people who can't quite speak a language very well.

I haven't used Duo Lingo for a new language yet, but I did use it for a while to brush up on my Italian and found it pretty useful.

As far as other free resources, there are a lot of language podcasts. It's only audio so it's not as extensive (for lack of a better word), but it can definitely be helpful too. I don't know any Spanish ones off the top of my head, but you can do a search in iTunes or Stitcher and find the one that's right for you

Keep in mind that they have Castilian Spanish as opposed to Latin American Spanish.

I like Duolingo, it is really good at what it's made for. But you need to keep in mind that what it's made for is reading comprehension and nothing else. Duolingo will not (and isn't supposed to) teach you how to speak a language. It's pretty bad for listening comprehension as well. Hell, I even turned off the speaking lessons in settings just because they are useless.

In my opinion, Duolingo is great for what it's made for but it shouldn't ever be used as a main form of learning; only supplementary.

Keep in mind that they have Castilian Spanish as opposed to Latin American Spanish.

I'm quite sure they have Latin American Spanish. They use the Spain flag because no South American country stands out or is easily recognizable, and the Mexican one is too similar to the Italian one.
